title: Where does a big number sit on a number line?
description: Farhan stops on a road with a distance stone at every twenty thousand metres. The video places his distance between two stones and compares the two gaps.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the two marks the number lies between, then compare the two gaps to see the nearer one. Watch for children who guess from the first digits.

source: Between which two marks of 0, 20,000, 40,000, 60,000 and 80,
video_script.why: The child can read big numbers but has not yet placed one between two marks on a number line.
video_script.substitution: Find the two marks that the number lies between, measure the gap to each, and the smaller gap shows the nearer mark.
video_script.anchor: Farhan on a long road with a distance stone at every twenty thousand metres out of his town
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu sees forty-seven, thinks it is nearly fifty, and says the number is nearer to sixty thousand. Fifty thousand is the middle, so the gaps must be measured, not guessed.
video_script.payoff_line: it is nearer to forty thousand

final_answer.spoken: between forty thousand and sixty thousand, nearer to forty thousand

never_show: the your-turn answer: between 20,000 and 40,000, nearer to 20,000
maths_rules: marks on the line: 0, 20,000, 40,000, 60,000, 80,000; each is 20,000 more than the one before
Farhan stops at 47,340 metres from the town
slip: 47 looks near 50, so Chintu says nearer to 60,000; but 50,000 is the middle mark and 47,340 is before it
video_script.design: One idea: a number sits between two marks and the smaller gap shows the nearer one. Wrong idea: judge nearness from the first digits. The road with stones stays as the anchor and turns into the number line.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='road'/>Farhan walks along a long road out of his town. A big stone stands at every twenty thousand metres.
<bookmark mark='stones'/>The stones read zero, twenty thousand, forty thousand, sixty thousand and eighty thousand.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Farhan stops at forty-seven thousand, three hundred and forty metres. Between which two stones is he, and which stone is nearer to him?

narration: <bookmark mark='more'/>Forty-seven thousand, three hundred and forty is more than forty thousand.
<bookmark mark='less'/>It is less than sixty thousand.
<bookmark mark='between'/>That means Farhan stands between the stone at forty thousand and the stone at sixty thousand.

narration: <bookmark mark='gapa'/>From forty thousand up to Farhan is seven thousand, three hundred and forty metres.
<bookmark mark='gapb'/>From Farhan up to sixty thousand is twelve thousand, six hundred and sixty metres.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Seven thousand, three hundred and forty is the smaller gap, so it is nearer to forty thousand.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Farhan sits between forty thousand and sixty thousand, nearer to forty thousand.
